Rs.2,15,600/- With Interest At The Rate Of 6% P.A. From
The Date Of Petition Till Realization.

These Appeals Having Been Heard And Reserved For
Judgment And Coming On For Pronouncement Of
Judgment This Day Through Video Conferening At
Kalaburgi, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
MFA No.7910/2018 by the petitioner and MFA No. 5984/2018 by the Insurance Company
are directed against the judgment and award dated 10-05-2018 passed in MVC No.776/2016 by the learned Principal Senior civil Judge and CJM and Member, Additional MACT, Hassan.

2. By the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,15,600/- as compensation to the petitioner together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

It is the case of the petitioner that on 07/02/2016 he was returning from the house of one Venkatesh situated at Agalahalli Village, Hassan taluk after seeing the ginger seeds, at about 4.15 p.m. he boarded the Bajaj Passenger Auto bearing registration No.KA-13-A-9335 at Agalahalli gate.
At about 4.30 p.m. near Ragimuddanahalli, the driver of the said Auto drove the same in rash and negligent manner, lost control of the vehicle and it skid and turned turtle.
As a result the petitioner fell on the road and Auto fell on his leg and he sustained grievous injuries to his left leg and 3 toes were cut off.

Immediately, the passengers travelling in the said Auto brought him to the Government Hospital, Hassan in another vehicle, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for one week, undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.50,000/- for medical expenses.

Earlier to accident, he was hale and healthy and earning Rs.25,000/- per month from agriculture and business and due to accidental injuries he is unable to attend the work as before and is depending upon his family members.

It was contended that the accident has taken place due to rash and NC: 2023:KHC:40576 negligent driving Auto bearing No.KA-13-A-9335 by its driver and it belongs to respondent No.1 and said vehicle is insured with respondent No.2.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to him.

Therefore, he prays for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest at 18%
per annum from the date of petition till realization.
4. On issuance of notice of the petition by the Tribunal, the respondent No.1 did not appear and he was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2- Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed objections denying the entire petition averments regarding age, occupation and income of the petitioner as well as narration of accident contended by the petitioner and contended that there is delay of more than 24 hours in lodging the complaint, which pre-supposes that not only the vehicle Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
3 is fixed, but also the version of the accident is changed by playing fraud against the company in collusion with the police authorities and respondent No.1.

The reason assigned for non filing of the NC: 2023:KHC:40576 complaint well within time is neither genuine nor bonafide but the same is after thought so as to defraud the insurance company; that the hospital authorities having admitted the petitioner, ought to have informed the police authorities immediately as it is a Medico Legal case.

However, the respondent No.2- Insurance Company admits issuance of policy to the Bajaj Passenger Auto bearing registration No.KA-13-A-9335 and seeks protection U/S 149(2) of M.V Act,
also enable to contest the claim on negligence and on quantum notwithstanding the stipulations.
Further, it was contended that the respondent No.1 has not submitted the DL of the driver who was driving the Bajaj Passenger Auto bearing No.KA-13-A-9335 at the material time of accident for the verification of respondent No.2 as per condition of the policy.

Further the petition is bad for non-compliance of Section 158(6) of M.V Act, in forwarding all the relevant documents to the concerned insured within 30 days from the date of the information but the Rural Police Station,
Hassan failed to forward the documents and not complied with the statutory demand.

As per Section 134 of M.V Act the NC: 2023:KHC:40576 respondent No.1/insurer herein to furnish the particulars of policy, date, time and place of accident, particulars of injured and the name of driver and particulars of the driving licence, but same is not furnished by respondent No.1.

The amount of compensation claimed at Rs.8,00,000/- is highly excessive, speculation and whimsical and not in consonance with the status, standard and nature of the injuries said to have been sustained by the petitioner.
Therefore, respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition with costs.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed appropriate issues and petitioner examined himself as PW1 and marked Exs.P1 to P24 and examined one witness as PW2 and marked Exs.P25 to P28 in evidence.
Respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW1 and Ex.R1 was marked in evidence.

6. The Tribunal after hearing both the sides and after considering the material on record, has partly allowed the petition and directed the Insurance Company to pay a NC: 2023:KHC:40576 sum of Rs.2,15,600/- as compensation to the petitioner under different heads as below:
Loss of income due to disability Rs.1,38,600/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 15,000/-
 Attender charges Rs. 15,000/-
Food and nourishment charges Rs. 15,000/-

Loss of income during treatment period Rs. 7,000/-
 Total Rs.2,15,600/-
7.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner has approached this Court in MFA No. 7910/2018.

He contends that the impugned judgment and award has overlooked the severity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the 3rd, 4th and 5th toes had been amputated and there was a degloving injury which has resulted in crippling of the petitioner.

It is contended that the compensation awarded Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
4 by the Tribunal is abysmally low and it has not considered the sufferings of the petitioner.
It is contended that the disability was also not properly assessed and therefore, the compensation deserves to be enhanced.

Against the same judgment and award, the Insurance Company has approached this Court in MFA No.5984/2018 contending that, inspite of the respondent No.1 had denied that the auto rickshaw has not involved in the accident, the Tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence in a proper manner.

It is contended that the affidavit filed before the Medical Authority succeeded in getting the entries made in the MLC records to the effect that the injuries suffered by the petitioner were owing to the road traffic accident and there is a delay in filing the FIR and none of the occupants of the said auto rickshaw has sustained injuries and therefore, the Tribunal was not justified in holding that there was an accident involving the auto rickshaw.

It is contended that the Tribunal should have noticed the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Rajendra Singh and others1 and in the case of Anil and others Vs.
AIR 2000 SC 1165 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 New India Assurance Company Limited2.

sentences.text: Hence, it has sought for absolving the liability on the insurance Company.
9. On issuance of notice by this Court, the rival parties have appeared through their counsel and arguments by both the sides were heard and the Tribunal records have been perused.
10. The Insurance Company is challenging the impugned judgment on the ground that the involvement of the said auto rickshaw in the alleged accident has not been properly considered by the Tribunal.

11. The learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company Sri A.N.Krishna Swamy, contends that, the MLC Register Extract produced by the Insurance Company goes to show that the involvement of the auto rickshaw in the accident was subsequently entered in the MLC records by virtue of an affidavit.

Therefore, it is contended that there is a delay of one day in filing the complaint and none of the other inmates of the auto rickshaw had sustained any injury 2018 ACJ 79 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 and therefore, the accident involving the auto rickshaw is doubtful.

12. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contend that there is no delay in filing the complaint, petitioner has sustained injuries and immediately he was shifted to the hospital and there was no necessity for the petitioner to file any affidavit, but in view of the insistence by the Medical Authorities, he might have filed an affidavit, based on which, the accident might have been Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
5 mentioned in the MLC Register Extract.

13. The perusal of FIR and the complaint produced at Exs.P1 and P2, disclose that the petitioner had given statement before the Police Constable while he was in the hospital on 8-2-2016 at about 7.00 p.m.
The complaint mention that the driver of the auto rickshaw while trying to avoid a pothole, lost control over the vehicle, it skid and turned turtle.
He states that his left foot was injured in the accident and three toes have been amputated.
He has stated that the public who had gathered there had sent him to the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 hospital and he has sought for action against the auto rickshaw driver.
The FIR was received by the police at about 7.45 p.m. on 8-2-2016 while the petitioner was taking treatment in the hospital.
Obviously, there is a delay of about 24 hours in filing the complaint.

The police intimation is produced at Ex.P8 by the petitioner and it shows that as per the affidavit dated 8-2-2016 the Government Hospital, Hassan, has issued an intimation to the police and it was received by the police before the petitioner gave statement as per Ex.P2 i.e. on 8-2-2016 at 7.00 p.m.
In the said police intimation, it is mentioned that the petitioner had approached the hospital with history that there was a toppling of the auto rickshaw near Agalahalli on 7-2-2016.
The discharge summary also mention that there was toppling of auto rickshaw on 7-2-2016 and the petitioner was treated for the injuries sustained in the accident.

14. Ex.P25 is the MLC Register Extract, wherein, it is mentioned that on 7-2-2016, the auto rickshaw had turned turtle and in the said accident, the petitioner has sustained - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 the injuries.
In the margin of Ex.P25, there is a mention that an affidavit was also filed by the petitioner.
It is relevant to note that there was no necessity for the Medical authorities to insist for an affidavit, but it is not known under what circumstances, they had insisted for the affidavit.
The summary sheet of the hospital is also produced at Ex.P26 and it shows that the petitioner had approached the hospital with the history of toppling over the auto rickshaw on 7-2-2016 at 4.00 p.m.

There is no evidence on record to show that the case sheet was also manipulated and it was written only on the next date i.e. on 8-2-2016.
15.

On a careful perusal of the above records, even though the police intimation as well as the MLC extract show that an affidavit was filed by the petitioner on 8-2-2016 reporting the accident, it cannot be said that there is a manipulation of the incident.

After the investigation, the police have filed the chargesheet as per Ex.P3 and therefore, the police records including the affidavit of PW1 should have been effectively rebutted by the Insurance Company in order - 14 - Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:40576 to succeed in the matter.

There being no such efforts made by the Insurance Company to rebut the available evidence on record, the deposition by its Official who was not at all an eye witness of the accident cannot be sufficient enough to hold that its version has been probabalised.
16. The second contention of the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company is that, none of the other inmates of the auto rickshaw had sustained any injury.
It is not necessary that every passenger who was in the auto rickshaw should have sustained injuries in the accident when the vehicle turned turtle.
Obviously, the petitioner had sustained the amputation of three toes of his left foot in the accident and it appears that he was sitting on the left side of the auto rickshaw.
Obviously, none other could have sustained any injury if they only fall on the petitioner who was on the left side.
Under these circumstances, this argument by learned counsel appearing for the Insurance company is not sustainable.
Hence, I am unable to accept - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company that there was no such accident.
17. The petitioner has also approached this Court in appeal contending that the compensation awarded is inadequate.
The Tribunal has appreciated the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in para 11 of the impugned judgment.

The petitioner has sustained amputation of the 3rd,
4th and 5th toes with degloving injury as may be seen from the medical records produced by him.
The photograph of the petitioner is also produced at Exs.P22 and P23 which show that three toes of his left leg have been amputated.
The medical records also show that there was such amputation with crush injury.
The evidence of PW2, who has assessed the disability also show that there was a disability of 11% to his left lower limb.

Even then the Tribunal considering the nature of the avocation stated by the petitioner that he was an agriculturist and owned agricultural lands as evidenced by the Record of Rights produced at Exs.P13 to P21, came to the conclusion that - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 there is a functional disability of 11%.
It is worth to note that though the Medical Officer states about the physical disability of a particular limb, the functional disability has to be assessed by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has assessed the same in detail with reference to the avocation of the petitioner and has come to the conclusion that 11% disability also applies to the functional disability and therefore, it has adopted the multiplier of '15' for the age of 36 years and has calculated the compensation under the head of 'loss of income due to disability'.
18.
While assessing the income of the petitioner, it has considered the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.7,000/- p.m. in the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the income.
The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalat prescribe a notional income of Rs.9,500/- per month for the year 2016.

In umpteen number of decisions including the decision in the case of Smt. Mariyamma Vs. Suyambulingam V and Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
7 - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 another,3

entities.text:
Smt. Mariyamma Vs. Suyambulingam V and Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
7 - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Division Bench of this Court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act and therefore, it can be accepted.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.9,500/- per month and hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 15 x 11%=1,88,100/-.

19. The Tribunal has considered the compensation under the head of 'pain and sufferings' at Rs.25,000/-, 'attendant charges' at Rs.15,000/-, 'food and nourishment charges' at Rs.15,000/- and 'loss of income during the laid up period' at Rs.27,000/-.
20.

Considering the nature of the injuries, the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period' has to be enhanced for a period of three months and therefore, a sum of Rs.28,500/- (9,500/- x 3) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

So far as 'loss of amenities' is considered, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- only,
even though there was amputation of three toes of the left leg of the petitioner.
Therefore, the compensation under the head of 'loss of amenities in life' needs to be enhanced.
Obviously, the amputation of the toes results in abnormal gait and therefore, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the remaining heads do not require any enhancement.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,21,600/- under the following heads:
Loss of income due to disability Rs.1,88,100/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Attendant charges Rs. 15,000/-
Food and nourishment charges Rs. 15,000/-

Loss of income during treatment period Rs. 28,500/-
 Total Rs.3,21,600/-
 Less:

Awarded by Tribunal Rs.2,15,600/-
 Enhancement Rs.1,06,000/-
23.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,06,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company deserves to be dismissed and the appeal filed by Paramesha vs Manjunatha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173999533/
8 - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:40576 the petitioner deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No. 7910/2018 filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.
(ii) MFA No.5984/2018 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.

(iii) The judgment and award passed in MVC No.776/2016 on 10-05-2018 by the Tribunal is modified, by awarding a sum of Rs.1,06,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within four weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
(v) The amount in deposit in MFA No.5984/ 2018 shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
